body: Worker rule (Termal::BarA2, 2026-10-23 10:52Z; my own incident). In a Bash-tool command, never put backticks inside a double-quoted argument (for example grep -E "warning: `termal`"). bash command-substitutes them. Here it ran target/release/termal (on PATH), which tried to start a second TermAl server and refused only because the live host holds the ~/.termal lock. For patterns that contain literal backticks or $, use single quotes, or match without the backticks (for example 'generated [0-9]+ warnings'). Read every filter pattern for `, $( and $VAR before running it.
